Portrait of Kiingi Taawhiao (Tukaroto Matutaera Potatau Te Wherowhero Tawhiao c.1822-1894) with tā moko (face tattoo) and wearing kahu kiwi (kiwi feather cloak) and ear pendant. Tāwhiao was leader of the Waikato tribes, the second Māori King, and a religious figure. He was a member of the Ngati Mahuta hapū of Waikato.
[Image vignetted and details retouched.]

View of Maori display at the London Colonial and Indian Exhibition 1886. Pataka (store house) front with carved panels and gable boards, three figures dressed in cloaks, other examples of carving mounted on walls. Flags hanging behind.

Full length posed portrait of two seated Maori girls, with their hands across their waists and draped across each other. They are wearing long dresses with shawls draped over their shoulders, and both have carved greenstone (jadeite) necklaces - one is clearly figure-shaped (a Hei tiki).

A group of people standing on the verandah of a wooden house, coming to sell 'curios'. On the right is a European man, standing. On his right is Tamati Takarangi, a Maori chief, wearing a long cloak with hanging black threads and carrying a staff or club (mostly hidden). Seated in a chair is a Maori woman wearing a dress with a scarf wrapped around her head. Seated further along the porch, in the doorway to the house, is an elderly Maori man wearing European style clothing, and holding a ?staff. Partially obscured at the left of the photograph is another elderly Maori man wearing European style clothing.

Portrait of a Maori man called Te Heuheu Tukino IV, chief of the Ngāti Tuwharetoa, a Maori tribe of the central North Island, who has a moko (facial tattoo) and is wearing a cloak decorated with feathers, captioned (in negative) 'Te Heu Heu - At Tokaanu - King Country'.  He is holding a patu (short-handled club) and is wearing an ear pendant of greenstone (jade of the nephrite kind, or pounamo in Maori).
Portrait of a Maori woman, a tourist guide, named Te Paea Hinerangi - known, more famously, as 'Guide Sophia' - standing outside a thatched hut, captioned (in negative) '"Sophia" - At Whakarewarewa'.

Group of Maori male prisoners seated on the ground with six soldiers (?militia) standing above them. Most of the Maori prisoners are wearing hats and some are wearing cloaks, blankets, or piupiu (a grass skirt). The soldiers are wearing uniforms, some with shoulder sashes, and carrying rifles. The photograph may have been taken during the East Cape War of 1865-1868, an anti-European uprising in the region.

Anthropometric, full length, full face portrait of a part-Maori man. He is standing with one hand across his abdomen. Godeffroy catalogue states that he came to Hamburg as a sailor and was photographed (and measured) there.
View of gallery in Auckland Museum showing Maori carved houses 'Te puawai a te Arawa(u?)
Group of men, women and children (including half-cast boys) in Maori dress outside house of raupo (bulrush) type with wooden and corrugated iron addition.

Group portrait of Maori men, women and children, standing and sitting on the ground, pictured on the shore of Lake Tarawera, at the settlement of Te Ariki, with Mount Tarawera visible in the distance, captioned (in negative) 'Te Ariki - Lake Tarawera. (Mount Tarawera.)'.

View of the roofs of three buildings, identified as Maori houses ('Whares') at Te Wairoa (also known as 'The Buried Village'), located close to the shore of Lake Tarawera, near Rotorua, nearly completely buried by mud and volcanic ash, photographed some time after the widespread destruction caused by the eruption of Mount Tarawera on 10 June 1886, captioned (in negative) 'Buried Whares - Wairoa - After Eruption - June 10 - 86'.
Maori carvings at a model 'pa' (Maori fortified village)

Group portrait of Maori men, women and children, standing and sitting, pictured between several houses at Pipiriki, a settlement on the east bank of the Whanganui River, captioned (in negative) 'Pipiriki - Wanganui River - King Country'.

Studio portrait of Makereti, wearing a korowai (tagged cloak) and two older women relatives, on left, Tiripa (aunt), and on right, Pia Ngarotu Te Rihi (mother), with moko (tattoo) wearing kahu kiwi (kiwi feather cloak).  All wear huia feathers in their hair and greenstone tikis.  Painted studio backdrop of folliage, and urn on pedestal and cloaks has been retouched to hide European clothing and chairs.
View of Maori objects, captioned (in negative) 'Maori Curios Kawau'.

A Maori tangi (funeral) with group mourning woman's body on left side of porch outside raupo (reed) house. The body is decorated with a head wreath of leaves and black ribbon, and positioned under sheets and black cloth onto which a greenstone mere (club) is laid.  The body is propped up on woven mats, with korowai (tag cloaks) hanging behind on porch wall.  A woman wearing in European clothing with blanket as over-skirt, sits in attendance.  Standing watching are three men, one in European clothing, one with a blanket as cloak, and the third wearing a korowai and flax cloaks.

View of several Maori men and a child, standing and sitting, pictured in front of a whare (house), apparently gathered for a funeral (tangihana or, more commonly, tangi) at Tieke, a settlement on the Whanganui River, captioned (in negative) 'A Tangi - Ti Eke - King Country' .
Maori toi moko (Preserved head with tattoos).
View of a painted tiki, or large wooden carving, captioned (in negative) 'Tiki (Maori God)'.
Exterior view of a Maori whare (house) with elaborately carved and painted wooden decoration, captioned (in negative) '"Uenuku" - "Matene Tehuaki's" House - Maketu'.

Interior view of a Maori whare rūnanga (meeting house), known as the Hinemihi meeting house, at the settlement of Te Wairoa, located close to the shore of Lake Tarawera, near Rotorua, captioned (in negative) 'Runanga House - Hinemihi Wairoa'.
